subject: CpG Islands identified as single Nucleotides

messages.author: e68b4574268abff2
messages.subject: CpG Islands identified as single Nucleotides
parts:
Hello,

Why does the start and end of the CpG Islands occur at the same nucleotide? Shouldn't there be a wider range that would be identified as a region? 
I have posted my code and my data results below. Thanks! 



library(methylKit)

# Set working directory
wpath <- "~/Desktop/diff_analysis"
setwd(wpath)

files <- list.files(path = wpath, pattern = "\\.bam$", full.names = TRUE)

# Create an empty list to store the processed methylRaw objects
methRaw_list <- list()

# Iterate over each file path and process them individually
for (i in seq_along(files)) {
  # Reading the methylation calls from sorted Bismark alignments
  methRaw <- processBismarkAln(
    location = files[i],  # Specify the current file path
    sample.id = paste0("test", i),  # Generate sample ID dynamically
    assembly = "mm10",
    #save.context = c("CpG", "CHG", "CHH"),
    read.context = "CpG",
    #save.folder = getwd()
  )
 
  # Append the processed methylRaw object to the list
  methRaw_list[[i]] <- methRaw
}

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] CpG Islands identified as single Nucleotides
parts:
they are not CpG islands, but CpG di-nucleotides, you can read a bit about how CpG islands are defined and what bisulfite sequencing or alike measures. This will clear up the confusion 

Best,
Altuna
